title: Investigate and patch asymmetric TTFT anomaly during multi-variant model fanout
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private tiers reported a sudden asymmetric regression in first-token latency (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec drop when requests are routed with multi-variant fanout (A/B routing to heterogeneous model variants). The regression is not uniform: single-variant routes are unaffected; mixed-variant fanout consistently shows 2x-5x TTFT and 30-60% tokens/sec degradation for requests that touch >1 model variant within a single request. Initial hypothesis: interactions between cross-variant KV prefetch, kernel selection heuristics, and weight-streaming serialization create head-of-line stalls and excessive lock contention in the runtime multiplexing layer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the fanout router to split traffic 50/50 between model-v1-int8 and model-v2-fp16 for a chat-style streaming request with context length ~1024 tokens.
2) Send sustained load at 50 concurrent sessions with mixed prompt lengths (50%-long), observe CPU/GPU utilization and per-request trace IDs.
3) Compare TTFT and tokens/sec against same traffic sent to a single pinned-variant route.
4) Reproduce in Hosted (us-west), Dedicated pool DP-4, and a Private VPC instance with identical model binaries to confirm cross-env nature.
observed_metrics: - TTFT median increased from ~60ms to 140-300ms for mixed-variant fanout paths
- Tokens/sec dropped from baseline 420 tps to 170-300 tps for affected requests
- GPU utilization remains high but shows frequent stalls; context-switch counters spike on the runtime threads
- KV cache miss rate increased by ~18% for requests that traversed variant boundaries
diagnostic_findings: - Traces show inflight requests often waiting on 'kernel_selection' and 'prefetch_lock' spans when they include multi-variant calls
- Kernel selector heuristics sometimes choose mixed-precision optimized kernels that require synchronous weight materialization, leading to stalls when weights are not resident
- Cross-variant prefetch attempts to stream weights for both variants concurrently, which can saturate the PCIe / NVLink scheduler and cause eviction churn
- Dedicated pools exhibit worse tail behavior because the scheduler batches mixed-precision requests into a single execution path more aggressively
- Private deployments show similar behavior but with longer warmup due to cold caches on air-gapped updates
short_term_mitigation: 1) Roll out conservative kernel selection override: force 'safe_serial' kernel path for requests that will fanout to >1 variant. This avoids concurrent weight streaming. (Canary 10% hosted -> monitor)
2) Disable cross-variant prefetch for high-priority customer tiers until memory-streaming backpressure logic is hardened
3) Apply a transient routing rule: prefer single-variant fallbacks for requests with long context lengths (>800 tokens) for the next 48 hours
4) Notify affected customers with status update and recommended temporary config (pin to single variant or lower fanout).
long_term_workplan: - Implement per-variant weight streaming rate limiter and backpressure-aware prefetch queue to prevent eviction churn
- Extend kernel selection heuristics to be aware of multi-variant fanout and expected memory residency
- Add an adaptive shedder that can detect cross-variant weight storms and gracefully downgrade to single-variant execution
- E2E test suite for mixed-variant fanout scenarios including Private air-gapped upgrades
- Postmortem and SLA impact reconciliation with Billing/Support teams
rollout_plan: - Stage 0 (now): apply kernel override patch to canary fleet (10% hosted region us-west) and 1 Dedicated pool (DP-2) for smoke tests
- Stage 1 (24h): expand to 50% of hosted traffic and 3 Dedicated pools if metrics stable
- Stage 2 (48-72h): offer patch to Private customers as hotfix build and provide migration guidance
- Rollback criteria: >10% customer error-rate increase, tokens/sec below baseline by >20% on canary, or any unhandled OOMs
- Monitoring: TTFT p50/p95, tokens/sec, KV miss rate, runtime stall spans; dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/fanout-ttft (internal)
